segments.quote: How do you handle things.thoughts like “Uh, oh, I’ve got a cold. This might be the beginning of the end”?

four_sides.factual: Gives an example of a small symptom read as the start of dying.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a hair-trigger threat reading of ordinary illness.
four_sides.relationship: Assumes peers recognise the thought.
four_sides.appeal: Asks how to manage that reaction.

segments.why: Quotes a mind jumping from a cold to the end, the catastrophising named.

segments.quote: Do you have a type of survivor’s guilt?

four_sides.factual: Asks whether others carry survivor's guilt.
four_sides.self_revelation: Hints at guilt about still being alive.
four_sides.relationship: Seeks company in the feeling.
four_sides.appeal: Asks for confirmation that the feeling is shared.

segments.why: Reaches toward others over an unspoken guilt, the need for company named.

segments.quote: I have a fantastic support system, my chosen family are beyond fantastic and loving yet, I'm feeling a bit sorry for myself and Lonely.

four_sides.factual: States that the support is excellent and loneliness is present anyway.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a feeling admitted despite having no justification for it.
four_sides.relationship: Credits the chosen family before naming the gap.
four_sides.appeal: Asks that the loneliness be heard without correction.

segments.why: Names loneliness alongside gratitude, the separation distress owned.

segments.quote: I've got stage 4 breast cancer that has metastasized to other parts of my body. It's terminal and I'm under home hospice care.

four_sides.factual: Gives the diagnosis, spread and care setting.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows the facts stated without softening.
four_sides.relationship: Gives readers the context plainly.

segments.why: States diagnosis and care arrangements as flat information.

segments.quote: I can still do most of what I used to do, I just tire very easily.

four_sides.factual: Describes retained ability limited by fatigue.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a measured appraisal of capacity.
four_sides.relationship: Corrects any picture of total incapacity.
four_sides.appeal: Asks not to be seen as helpless.

segments.why: Assesses remaining capacity evenly without charge.

segments.quote: I keep my mind and hands busy. I spin my own fleece, knit, crochet, paint, draw etc.

four_sides.factual: Lists the crafts that occupy her.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows appetite still alive and directed into making.
four_sides.relationship: Shows readers a full life rather than an empty one.
four_sides.appeal: Asks readers to see the activity.

segments.why: Lists ongoing making, the drive and the creativity both engaged.

segments.quote: I've "blinged" out my canes and I'm working on my walker now!

four_sides.factual: Describes decorating mobility aids.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows humour and style applied to the equipment of decline.
four_sides.relationship: Invites readers to enjoy the flourish.
four_sides.appeal: Asks readers to share the fun.

segments.why: Turns medical equipment into a craft project, playfulness expressed openly.

segments.quote: Yet, here I am balling my eyes out when I could just phone any family member and talk. UGH!

four_sides.factual: Reports crying alone despite available company.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows frustration at her own inability to reach out.
four_sides.relationship: Confesses to readers what she has not said to family.
four_sides.appeal: Asks readers to understand the impasse.

segments.why: Reports crying that floods out while the offered support goes unaccepted.

segments.quote: Terminal cancer & stable but I can’t stop feeling negative.

four_sides.factual: States a stable terminal condition and persistent negative feeling.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a state she cannot shift by will.
four_sides.relationship: Presents the problem to readers as a puzzle.
four_sides.appeal: Asks for help with the mood.

segments.why: Reports a mood that will not lift, the forward pull absent despite good news.

segments.quote: My doctor said I had 12 to 18 months to live.

four_sides.factual: Reports the prognosis given.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows the number retained precisely.
four_sides.relationship: Places the doctor as the source of the verdict.

segments.why: Reports a prognosis as plain information.

segments.quote: But here I am, 2 years later and I have been stable for 9 months now. I hadn’t even known being stable was a possibility!

four_sides.factual: Notes outliving the prognosis and a stability she did not know existed.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows surprise at an outcome nobody prepared her for.
four_sides.relationship: Implies the clinicians never offered this possibility.
four_sides.appeal: Asks readers to register the reprieve.

segments.why: Registers an unexpected opening, the surprise stated with some lift.

segments.quote: So, I should be absolutely jumping for joy! Every day is a bonus.

four_sides.factual: States the reaction she believes is expected of her.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a gap between the prescribed feeling and the actual one.
four_sides.relationship: Anticipates readers who would tell her to be glad.
four_sides.appeal: Asks that the shortfall be forgiven.

segments.why: Names an expected elation that does not arrive, the appetite not mobilising.

segments.quote: My problem is I just cannot shake off these negative thoughts I’m having.

four_sides.factual: Identifies persistent negative thinking as the problem.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows effort against the thoughts that keeps failing.
four_sides.relationship: Presents the difficulty for readers to weigh in on.
four_sides.appeal: Asks for a way to shift it.

segments.why: Reports repeated failure to shift a stuck state, the drive foreclosed.

segments.quote: When I’m feeling pretty rough I almost wish it was all over with.

four_sides.factual: Admits wishing for the end on bad days.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows exhaustion reaching toward an ending.
four_sides.relationship: Trusts readers with an admission likely to alarm.
four_sides.appeal: Asks not to be alarmed at.

segments.why: Reaches toward an end rather than forward, the appetite collapsed.

segments.quote: I’m so tired of fighting and pretending I’m feeling much better than I actually am.

four_sides.factual: States exhaustion at both the fight and the performance of wellness.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a mask acknowledged and resented.
four_sides.relationship: Implicates the people the pretending is for.
four_sides.appeal: Asks to be released from performing.

segments.why: Names swallowed resentment at having to perform, with the drive to keep fighting spent.

segments.quote: When I put the Christmas decorations away I’m wondering if I’ll be here to put them up next year.

four_sides.factual: Describes an annual task shadowed by doubt about being alive.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows ordinary routine converted into a countdown.
four_sides.relationship: Lets readers into a private moment.
four_sides.appeal: Asks readers to feel the shadow over daily life.

segments.why: Names a routine turned into a reckoning about being alive next year.

segments.quote: I can’t believe my luck so far and I’m dreading every oncologist visit as I’m scared of hearing the news that I’m no longer stable.

four_sides.factual: States dread of appointments and fear of losing stability.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows good news held as something about to be taken back.
four_sides.relationship: Casts the oncologist visit as the source of threat.
four_sides.appeal: Asks readers to understand the dread.

segments.why: Dreads each appointment in advance, the threat running ahead of any news.

segments.quote: My husband is now talking about a few days away for the summer holidays and I should be all excited and planning them but all I can think of is Well, I can’t do this excursion because I’ll be too tired, I can’t do that one as it’s up a hill, etc.

four_sides.factual: Reports a proposed trip met only by lists of what she cannot do.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows anticipation replaced by inventory of limits.
four_sides.relationship: Positions the husband as hopeful and herself as the drag.
four_sides.appeal: Asks readers to see why the excitement will not come.

segments.why: Meets an offered plan with foreclosure, no anticipation mobilising.

segments.quote: It’s like I just don’t see the point. I’ve always been very active and adventurous.

four_sides.factual: States the loss of any sense of point, against a former active self.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a self she no longer recognises.
four_sides.relationship: Asks readers to measure the change.
four_sides.appeal: Asks for the loss to be understood.

segments.why: Says the point is gone while naming the lost former self.

segments.quote: Now I’ll just spoil things for my husband.

four_sides.factual: Predicts ruining the trip for her husband.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows self-blame for a burden she believes she imposes.
four_sides.relationship: Casts herself as a liability to the person she loves.
four_sides.appeal: Asks to be contradicted.

segments.why: Turns concern for the husband into self-blame, the tending curdled into burden.

segments.quote: Hello! I’m 24f This is my first time posting in this group but I’ve had cancer for about 4 years now with 2 recurrences and I’ve officially been diagnosed as terminal.

four_sides.factual: Introduces herself with age, history and terminal status.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows the facts delivered in a cheerful, unguarded register.
four_sides.relationship: Enters the group as a newcomer greeting the room.
four_sides.appeal: Asks to be received.

segments.why: Introduces herself to a group while naming a terminal diagnosis without weighting it.

segments.quote: I’m doing maintenance chemo but during my last appointment my doctor told me she expects that I have months to a year left.

four_sides.factual: Reports current treatment and the timeframe given.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows the prognosis relayed without visible flinch.
four_sides.relationship: Gives the group the facts it needs to answer her.

segments.why: Relays treatment and timeframe as plain information.

segments.quote: Weirdly enough I haven’t felt devastated or depressed necessarily. I feel a type of peace and acceptance with the whole thing

four_sides.factual: Reports peace and acceptance instead of devastation.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a settled state she finds strange in herself.
four_sides.relationship: Offers the group an unexpected report.
four_sides.appeal: Asks whether this is recognisable.

segments.why: Reports a settled state as observation, with no system driving the sentence.

segments.quote: the biggest bummer is that I kind of just get fomo lol…

four_sides.factual: Names missing out on future life as the main complaint.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows longing for life delivered with a light word and a laugh.
four_sides.relationship: Keeps the tone easy for the reader.
four_sides.appeal: Asks that the grief be taken lightly.

segments.why: Names the longing for a future life and softens it with a laugh.

segments.quote: I guess I’m just wondering if anyone else has felt this way about their own prognosis.

four_sides.factual: Asks whether others have felt similarly.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a wish to know she is not anomalous.
four_sides.relationship: Treats the group as a mirror.
four_sides.appeal: Asks for others to say so.

segments.why: Reaches for company in an experience while asking a genuine question.

segments.quote: I do have a wonderful support system that I had to build because I lost almost all my friends when I was first diagnosed in 2021.

four_sides.factual: States the support system was rebuilt after friends left.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a hard loss reported without accusation.
four_sides.relationship: Names the friends' departure without attacking them.
four_sides.appeal: Asks that the rebuilding be credited.

segments.why: Names abandonment by friends plainly, the loss stated without protest.

segments.quote: Im not afraid of death and I’m actually somewhat grateful that I know that I’ll be able to die in my own home surrounded by friends and family which is a privilege a lot of people don’t get.

four_sides.factual: States a lack of fear and gratitude for the circumstances of dying.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows gratitude reached from inside the situation.
four_sides.relationship: Compares her position favourably to others'.
four_sides.appeal: Asks readers to see the privilege as real.

segments.why: Values being surrounded by people at the end, warmth named as gratitude.

segments.quote: I just don’t understand why I’m not more upset.

four_sides.factual: States puzzlement about her own lack of distress.
four_sides.self_revelation: Shows a mind examining itself honestly.
four_sides.relationship: Hands the question over to the group.
four_sides.appeal: Asks for an explanation.

segments.why: Turns curiosity on her own reaction and asks for an answer.
